newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court tells Commission to look again at cartonboard fines.
newsitem.headline: Court tells Commission to look again at cartonboard fines.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance said on Thursday the European Commission should take another look at lifting fines for competition violation against some wood pulp manufacturers.

In 1993 the court reduced fines against some wood pulp manufacturers, and other fined companies who were not part of the original action have asked the court to require the Commission to reduce their fines.
The court has annulled in part a 1995 Commission decision refusing to reconsider the fines but did not direct the Commission as to what decision it should take now.

"The decision whether or not to withdraw the wood pulp decision, possibly ih part, is in the first place a matter for the Commission, which is required to carry out that assessment pursuant to article 176 of the EC treaty," the court said.
AssiDoman Kraft Products AB, AB Iggesunds Bruk, Korsnas AB, MoDo Paper AB, Sodra Cell AB, Stora Kopparbergs Bergslags AB, Svenska Cellulosa AB

application for annulment of the Commission's decision rejecting the requests made by the applicants, following the judgment of the Court of Justice in Joined Cases C-89/85, C-104/85, C-114/85, C-116/85 C-117/85 and C-125/85 Ahlstrom Osakeyhtio and Others v Commission (1993) ECR I-1307, for repayment of the fines imposed on them by Commission decision 85/202/EEC relating to a proceeding under article 85 of the EEC Treaty (IV/29.725 - Wood pulp)(OJ 1985 L 85, p. 1)

1. Annuls the Commission's decision, contained in the letter of 4 October 1995, rejecting the applicant's request that it review, in light of the judgment of the Court of Justice in Joined Cases C-89/85, C-104/85, C-114/85, C-116/85 C-117/85 and C-125/85 Ahlstrom Osakeyhtio and Others v Commission (1993) ECR I-1307, the legality of Commission deicision 85/202/EEC relating to a proceeding under article 85 of the EEC Treaty (IV/29.725 - Wood pulp) in so far as the latter relates to them;
2. Dismisses the action as inadmissible in so far as it seeks the issue of directions to the Commission;
3. Orders the Commission to pay the costs.
